sentences.l2: 远程办公的普及，让"工作"与"生活"之间原本清晰的边界逐渐变得模糊。
sentences.l1: The spread of remote work has gradually blurred the originally clear boundary between "work" and "life".

sentences.l2: 过去，通勤是一段缓冲：走出办公室的那一刻，人便正式下班，家庭时间由此开始。
sentences.l1: In the past, the commute was a buffer: the moment you walked out of the office, you were officially off work, and family time began from there.

sentences.l2: 然而，当办公桌被搬进客厅，这种切换也随之消失。
sentences.l1: However, when the office desk was moved into the living room, this switch disappeared too.

sentences.l2: 许多人虽然不必再到公司打卡，却发现自己几乎随时在线——清晨查看邮件，深夜回复钉钉上的消息，工作仿佛渗透进了生活的每一个缝隙。
sentences.l1: Although many people no longer have to go to the company to clock in, they find themselves online almost all the time: checking email at dawn, replying to messages on DingTalk late at night, with work seeming to seep into every crack of life.

sentences.l2: 这种状态看似自由，实则暗藏代价。
sentences.l1: This state seems free, but in fact it hides a cost.

sentences.l2: 当上级的消息可以在任何时刻抵达，员工便难以真正放松；大脑始终处于待命状态，休息的质量自然下降。
sentences.l1: When a superior's message can arrive at any moment, employees find it hard to truly relax; the brain is always on standby, and the quality of rest naturally declines.

sentences.l2: 更值得警惕的是，边界的消失常被包装成"灵活"与"高效"，让人在不知不觉中延长了劳动时间。
sentences.l1: More worrying still, the disappearance of boundaries is often packaged as "flexibility" and "efficiency", causing people to lengthen their working hours without realizing it.

sentences.l2: 因此，重建边界并非拒绝技术，而是学会为自己设定规则：哪些时段属于工作，哪些只属于家人和自己。
sentences.l1: Therefore, rebuilding boundaries is not about rejecting technology, but about learning to set rules for yourself: which hours belong to work, and which belong only to your family and yourself.

sentences.l2: 唯有如此，远程办公带来的才是自由，而非另一种束缚。
sentences.l1: Only in this way is what remote work brings freedom, rather than another kind of constraint.
